newsitem.title: ITALY: Montedison ordered to pay damages for dam.
newsitem.headline: Montedison ordered to pay damages for dam.

text.p: A court in the northeast Italian town of Belluno has ordered energy and agro-industry group Montedison to pay some 55 billion lire ($33 million) in damages to the town of Longarone which was largely destroyed when a dam overflowed in October 1963, Longarone's mayor said on Tuesday.
Some 2,000 people died in the disaster.

Mayor Gioacchino Bratti told Reuters the Belluno court had ordered Montedison to pay the Longarone municipal authorities 55.65 billion lire in compensation for "material and moral damages" caused in the so-called Vajont disaster.
There was no immediate comment from Montedison.
At the time the dam was built by the Societa' Adriatica di Elettricita' of the Edison company which is now over 60 percent controlled by Montedison.
Longarone's lawyer Claudio Consolo said Montedison could appeal against the sentence but the civil court ruling after a seven-year suit meant the damages had to be paid at some stage.
